audit.evidence: Real official deno release binaries 2.6.7/2.7.1/2.7.2 installed side-by-side via deno.land install.sh; minimal HTTP harness GET /probe?arg exercises transformDenoShellCommand inside the real binary; observed original flag@v0 blocked@v1, residual flag@v1 blocked@v2, original blocked@v2, passed:true.

app_purpose: Deno is a secure JavaScript/TypeScript/WebAssembly runtime shipped as a single self-contained binary. It provides a Node.js compatibility layer, including a `node:child_process` polyfill. When code spawns a subprocess with `shell: true` and the shell command begins with the Deno executable, Deno's `transformDenoShellCommand()` (ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts) re-parses the deno CLI arguments (to translate Node.js flags and inject `-A`) and RE-QUOTES them so they are 'safe to embed in a shell command string'. That per-argument shell-metacharacter neutralization is the security boundary: a real app that runs `deno` as a subprocess with `shell: true` and attacker-influenced arguments relies on it to prevent OS command injection / permission-system bypass.
root_cause_note: CWE-78 OS command injection via INCOMPLETE shell-metacharacter neutralization in the SAME sink, Deno's transformDenoShellCommand() for node:child_process shell:true. CVE-2026-27190 (fixed 2.6.8): transformDenoShellCommand() used an INCOMPLETE blocklist `/[();&|<>`!]/` and did NO quoting -- if a translated arg matched the blocklist the ORIGINAL command was returned unchanged (metachar reaches /bin/sh), and if it did not match, args were joined with no quoting; either way a live backtick executes a command substitution. The 2.6.8 fix (carried into 2.7.1) replaced this with per-arg SHELL-QUOTING. CVE-2026-32260 (fixed 2.7.2): that quoting has a PRIORITY bug -- its POSIX branch wraps any arg containing a `$VAR`/`${VAR}` reference in DOUBLE quotes (to preserve expansion) BEFORE the single-quote branch, and double quotes in POSIX sh do NOT suppress backtick command substitution, so a `$VAR`+backtick arg is double-quoted and the backtick still executes. Residual metacharacter evolution: plain backtick (V0->V1, closed by single-quoting) then $VAR-steered double-quoted backtick (V1->V2, closed by the `unsafeInDoubleQuotes` gate).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL NUANCE (verified against the REAL published deno release binaries 2.6.7 / 2.7.1 / 2.7.2 in-container, and against ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts at tags v2.6.7 / v2.7.1 / v2.7.2): both flaws live in the SAME sink `transformDenoShellCommand()` and are the SAME vuln class (per-arg shell-metacharacter neutralization for node:child_process shell:true, CWE-78). The mechanism EVOLVED across the two fixes: 2.6.7 used a blocklist-only approach with NO quoting (`if (/[();&|<>`!]/.test(arg)) return command; ... return prefix + ' ' + args.join(' ')`); the 2.6.8 fix rewrote this to per-arg SHELL-QUOTING (single-quote metachar args, but DOUBLE-quote `$VAR` args to preserve expansion); the 2.7.2 fix added `unsafeInDoubleQuotes = /`|\$\(|\\/` so a `$VAR` arg that ALSO contains a backtick/`$(`/backslash falls back to single-quoting. This case is Variant A (same SINK + same FLAG CHANNEL -- both injections flow through transformDenoShellCommand() -> /bin/sh command substitution and are detected as the planted secret appearing in the deno error output). The seed (plain backtick) and residual ($VAR+backtick) differ only in whether a `$VAR` prefix steers the arg into the vulnerable double-quote branch. The 2.7.x transform additionally routes args through the Rust ops op_node_parse_shell_args / op_node_translate_cli_args before quoting; the plain-backtick and $VAR+backtick args were both empirically confirmed to survive that path and reach the quoting branches as intended. SEED-EXPLOIT NUANCE: the injected backtick command substitution's output is interpolated into a deno CLI argument, so the flag is observed via deno's `Module not found "<flag>"` error on stderr (which echoes the substituted arg) -- this faithfully proves /canary/rf executed (on the blocked versions the LITERAL backtick, url-encoded %60, appears instead of the flag, so flag-in-output is a sound injection oracle).

flag.detect: flag token substring in the `output` field (stdout+stderr) of the probe result

sink: node:child_process spawnSync(`${Deno.execPath()} ${userArg}`, {shell:true}) -> Deno's transformDenoShellCommand() re-parses+re-quotes the deno CLI args -> /bin/sh -c. transformDenoShellCommand()'s per-arg shell-metacharacter neutralization is the boundary. If it leaves a backtick live (V0: no quoting; V1: $VAR arg double-quoted), /bin/sh runs the injected command substitution `/canary/rf` that reads the planted flag.
residual: On V1 (deno 2.7.1) the CVE-2026-27190 fix single-quotes metachar args, closing the plain-backtick seed. But transformDenoShellCommand()'s POSIX branch double-quotes any arg containing a `$VAR`/`${VAR}` reference BEFORE the single-quote branch, and double quotes in POSIX sh do not suppress backtick command substitution, so the arg `run $X`/canary/rf`` is double-quoted and the backtick still runs /canary/rf -> flag. The plain-backtick seed is blocked on V1; the $VAR-steered double-quoted backtick residual (CVE-2026-32260) is not. V2 (2.7.2) forces it into the single-quote branch via `unsafeInDoubleQuotes`.

evidence.fix_reference: deno 2.7.1 (official release binary; carries the CVE-2026-27190 fix from 2.6.8; still vulnerable to CVE-2026-32260, fixed in 2.7.2); deno 2.7.2 (official release binary; CVE-2026-32260 fix)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-32260 (CVSS 8.1): Deno 2.7.0-2.7.1 command injection in the node:child_process polyfill (shell: true). The two-stage argument sanitization in transformDenoShellCommand (ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts) has a priority bug: when an argument contains a $VAR pattern it is wrapped in double quotes instead of single quotes, and double quotes in POSIX sh do not suppress backtick command substitution, allowing injected commands to execute. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-27190. Fixed in 2.7.2.

provenance.notes: debian:bookworm-slim faithful-core; REAL official deno release binaries per version (2.6.7 / 2.7.1 / 2.7.2) installed side-by-side via the official install.sh, selected by HARNESS_VER so Deno.execPath() (hence the version-specific transformDenoShellCommand) is the exact published bytes. The harness drives the REAL Deno node:child_process shell:true path as an OS-command-injection sink: `<Deno.execPath()> <arg>` run via spawnSync(cmd, {shell:true}). Variant A incomplete-fix at the SAME sink transformDenoShellCommand(): V0 (2.6.7) leaves a plain backtick unescaped (incomplete blocklist + no quoting) -> command substitution runs /canary/rf -> flag; V1 (2.7.1) single-quotes plain-backtick args blocking the seed, but STILL double-quotes $VAR args and double quotes do not suppress backticks -> `run $X`/canary/rf`` runs /canary/rf -> flag = CVE-2026-32260 residual; V2 (2.7.2) forces $VAR+backtick args into the single-quote branch (unsafeInDoubleQuotes) -> blocked. Benign canary: injected command merely `cat /canary/flag.txt` (no real payload; derived from the advisories + source diff only). The mechanism was first confirmed empirically on the host with the same three official deno binaries, then gate-passed on real Docker. Gate passed on real Docker 2026-07-14.
